claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me **the name(s) of the child or children** you're inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to see if I can claim Child Benefit for my son, Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about Child Benefit for your son, **Alex**.

To assess your eligibility, I need to gather some details about your circumstances. Let me start with the first question:

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 8 years old - he was born in March 2017.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! So Alex was born in March 2017, making him 8 years old.

Next, I need to understand your living situation:

**Do you live in the UK, and if so, what is your residency status?** (For example, are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or on a visa?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Birmingham. I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for that clarification.

Now, I need to ask about your work and residency history:

**Have you been living in the UK for at least 2 of the last 3 years?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I've been living here my whole life.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. That confirms you meet the residency requirement.

Now I need to ask about your family circumstances:

**Are you the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is there another person (such as a partner or ex-partner) who might also be claiming or eligible to claim for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex doesn't actually live with me - he lives with his mum, my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's an important detail.

To help me understand the situation better:

**Does Alex's mum currently claim Child Benefit for him, or are you aware of whether she intends to claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure if she's claiming it or not, to be honest.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's understandable. Let me ask this another way:

**Who is the person with primary day-to-day care and responsibility for Alex?** (In other words, who does Alex live with and who makes the day-to-day decisions about his care, schooling, etc.?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: His mum has primary care - Alex lives with her full-time and she makes all the day-to-day decisions about his schooling and everything else.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's a key detail for assessing eligibility.

One more question to complete my assessment:

**Are you currently providing any financial support towards Alex's maintenance and upkeep** (such as regular payments to his mum for his care, food, clothing, etc.)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out. I contribute towards his clothes and things he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all of that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me carefully review the situation against the Child Benefit eligibility rules:

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 8 years old (born March 2017)
- You live in the UK and are a British citizen
- You've lived in the UK your whole life
- Alex's mum has primary day-to-day care and responsibility for Alex
- Alex lives with his mum full-time
- You contribute financially towards Alex's needs

Under Child Benefit rules, the person with **primary responsibility for the child** is generally the one eligible to claim. Since Alex's mum has primary day-to-day care and responsibility for Alex, and he lives with her full-time, she would be the person entitled to claim Child Benefit for him.

While you do contribute financially towards Alex's maintenance, this doesn't establish primary responsibility in the way required for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:**

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

The key reason is that Child Benefit is claimed by the person with primary day-to-day care and responsibility for the child. Since Alex lives with his mum full-time and she makes the day-to-day decisions about his care and schooling, she is the person who should claim Child Benefit for him.

If you'd like to discuss this further or if your circumstances change in the future, feel free to get in touch. If Alex's mum is not currently claiming Child Benefit, she may wish to look into whether she's eligible to do so.
